parse.title: Focus intensification
parse.wikitext:
<onlyinclude>
'''Focus intensification''' is defined as the experience of an increased ability to selectively concentrate on an aspect of the environment while ignoring other things. It can be best characterized by feelings of intense concentration which can allow one to continuously focus on and perform tasks which would otherwise be considered too monotonous, boring, or dull to not get distracted from.<ref name="FordSchroeder2008">{{cite journal|last1=Ford|first1=Jason A.|last2=Schroeder|first2=Ryan D.|title=Academic Strain and Non-Medical Use of Prescription Stimulants among College Students|journal=Deviant Behavior|volume=30|issue=1|year=2008|pages=26–53|issn=0163-9625|doi=10.1080/01639620802049900}}</ref><ref name="RiccioWaldrop2001">{{cite journal|last1=Riccio|first1=Cynthia A.|last2=Waldrop|first2=Jennifer J.M.|last3=Reynolds|first3=Cecil R.|last4=Lowe|first4=Patricia|title=Effects of Stimulants on the Continuous Performance Test (CPT)|journal=The Journal of Neuropsychiatry and Clinical Neurosciences|volume=13|issue=3|year=2001|pages=326–335|issn=0895-0172|doi=10.1176/jnp.13.3.326}}</ref>

The degree of focus induced by this effect can be much stronger than what a person is capable of sober. It can allow for hours of effortless, single-minded, and continuous focus on a particular activity to the exclusion of all other considerations such as eating and attending to bodily functions. However, although focus intensification can improve a person’s ability to engage in tasks and use time effectively, it is worth noting that it can also cause a person to focus intensely and spend excess time on unimportant activities. 

Focus intensification is often accompanied by other coinciding effects such as [[motivation enhancement]], [[thought acceleration]], and [[stimulation]]. It is most commonly induced under the influence of [[dosage#common|moderate]] [[dosage|dosages]] of [[stimulant]] and [[nootropic]] compounds such as [[amphetamine]],<ref name="SeidenSabol1993">{{cite journal|last1=Seiden|first1=L S|last2=Sabol|first2=K E|last3=Ricaurte|first3=G A|title=Amphetamine: Effects on Catecholamine Systems and Behavior|journal=Annual Review of Pharmacology and Toxicology|volume=33|issue=1|year=1993|pages=639–676|issn=0362-1642|doi=10.1146/annurev.pa.33.040193.003231}}</ref> [[methylphenidate]],<ref name="SpragueSleator1977">{{cite journal|last1=Sprague|first1=R.|last2=Sleator|first2=E.|title=Methylphenidate in hyperkinetic children: differences in dose effects on learning and social behavior|journal=Science|volume=198|issue=4323|year=1977|pages=1274–1276|issn=0036-8075|doi=10.1126/science.337493}}</ref> [[modafinil]],<ref name="RandallViswanath2005">{{cite journal|last1=Randall|first1=Delia C.|last2=Viswanath|first2=Aparna|last3=Bharania|first3=Punam|last4=Elsabagh|first4=Sarah M.|last5=Hartley|first5=David E.|last6=Shneerson|first6=John M.|last7=File|first7=Sandra E.|title=Does Modafinil Enhance Cognitive Performance in Young Volunteers Who Are Not Sleep-Deprived?|journal=Journal of Clinical Psychopharmacology|volume=25|issue=2|year=2005|pages=175–179|issn=0271-0749|doi=10.1097/01.jcp.0000155816.21467.25}}</ref> and [[caffeine]].<ref name="BernsteinCarroll1994">{{cite journal|last1=Bernstein|first1=Gail A.|last2=Carroll|first2=Marilyn E.|last3=Crosby|first3=Ross D.|last4=Perwien|first4=Amy R.|last5=Go|first5=Frances S.|last6=Benowitz|first6=Neal L.|title=Caffeine Effects on Learning, Performance, and Anxiety in Normal School-Age Children|journal=Journal of the American Academy of Child & Adolescent Psychiatry|volume=33|issue=3|year=1994|pages=407–415|issn=08908567|doi=10.1097/00004583-199403000-00016}}</ref> However, it is worth noting that the same compounds which induce this mind state at moderate dosages will also often result in the opposite effect of [[focus suppression]] at [[dosage#heavy|heavier]] dosages.<ref name="SaloNordahl2007">{{cite journal|last1=Salo|first1=Ruth|last2=Nordahl|first2=Thomas E.|last3=Natsuaki|first3=Yutaka|last4=Leamon|first4=Martin H.|last5=Galloway|first5=Gantt P.|last6=Waters|first6=Christy|last7=Moore|first7=Charles D.|last8=Buonocore|first8=Michael H.|title=Attentional Control and Brain Metabolite Levels in Methamphetamine Abusers|journal=Biological Psychiatry|volume=61|issue=11|year=2007|pages=1272–1280|issn=00063223|doi=10.1016/j.biopsych.2006.07.031}}</ref>
</onlyinclude>
